title: Vowel Harmony (Ahəng Qanunu)
subtitle: The foundational phonetic law governing all Azerbaijani suffixes
keyPoint: Azerbaijani suffixes harmonize with the preceding vowel by either a 2-way (-a/-ə) or 4-way (-ı/-i/-u/-ü) alternation rule.

mistakes.note: The root 'ev' contains the front vowel 'e', requiring front vowel suffix '-lər'.
The last vowel of 'qapı' is back 'ı', so the accusative must be '-nı', not '-ni'.
'ö' is a front vowel, so it takes '-lər' rather than '-lar'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'dost' (friend):
quiz.explanation: The vowel 'o' in 'dost' is back (qalın), requiring '-lar'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct accusative suffix for 'söz' (word):
quiz.explanation: 'ö' is front and rounded, so 4-way harmony selects '-ü'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural form of 'pəncərə' (window):
quiz.explanation: 'pəncərə' ends in front vowel 'ə', requiring '-lər'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct definite accusative form of 'qələm' (pen):
quiz.explanation: The last vowel in 'qələm' is front unrounded 'ə', taking '-i'.

tip: Always look strictly at the very LAST vowel in the stem to determine which suffix variant to attach.

title: Six-Case Noun Inflection
subtitle: Navigating core relational markers on Azerbaijani nouns
keyPoint: Azerbaijani nouns take one of six case suffixes depending on syntactic function, inserting buffer 'n' or 'y' after vowel-final stems.

mistakes.note: When the dative suffix '-a/-ə' attaches to a vowel-final stem like 'Bakı', buffer 'y' is required ('Bakıya').
'ev' has front vowel 'e', so locative must be '-də', not '-da'.
'masa' has back vowels, so ablative must be '-dan'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mən hər gün ___ gedirəm' (to work).
quiz.explanation: Destination requires the dative case ending '-ə' on the root 'iş'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Uşaqlar ___ oynayırlar' (in the park).
quiz.explanation: Stationary location requires the locative case suffix '-da'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Aygün ___ gəlir' (from school).
quiz.explanation: Direction away from/origin takes the ablative suffix '-dən'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Biz ___ yaşayırıq' (in Ganja - Gəncə).
quiz.explanation: 'Gəncə' ends in front vowel 'ə', taking locative '-də'.

tip: Remember that Locative (-da/-də) and Ablative (-dan/-dən) use buffer 'n' only after 3rd person possessive endings, but directly take '-da/-dan' after regular nouns.

title: Personal Predicative Suffixes (Xəbərlik Şəkilçiləri)
subtitle: Conjugating the present copular verb 'to be' directly onto stems
keyPoint: The Azerbaijani copula 'to be' attaches directly to predicates as personal suffixes following 4-way vowel harmony.

mistakes.note: When attaching 1st person '-əm' to a vowel-final stem like 'tələbə', buffer 'y' is compulsory: 'tələbəyəm'.
'yorğun' has rounded back vowel 'u', requiring rounded suffix '-uq'.
In negative copular sentences, the negative particle 'deyil' comes after the noun/adjective.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mən indi evdə___' (I am at home).
quiz.explanation: 1st person singular 'mən' requires '-yəm' after vowel 'ə'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Siz haralı___?' (Where are you from?).
quiz.explanation: 2nd person plural 'siz' takes '-sınız⁴' (here '-sınız' following 'ı').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Biz bu gün şad___' (We are glad).
quiz.explanation: 'Biz' (we) requires 1st person plural suffix '-ıq' to harmonize with back vowel 'a'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'O, həkim ___' (He is not a doctor).
quiz.explanation: Negation of noun/adjective predicates uses 'deyil' (often with 3rd person '-dir' or standalone 'deyil').

tip: In everyday spoken Azerbaijani, the 3rd person suffix '-dır/-dir/-dur/-dür' is frequently dropped, e.g. 'O yaxşıdır' often becomes 'O yaxşı'.

title: Possessive Suffixes (Mənsubiyyət Şəkilçiləri)
subtitle: Attaching ownership markers to items and forming genitive chains
keyPoint: Possession in Azerbaijani is marked directly on the possessed noun with personal endings, usually paired with genitive pronouns.

mistakes.note: For vowel stems, 1st person possessive suffix is simply '-m', not '-mım'.
Third-person possessive after a vowel requires the buffer 's', giving '-sı/-si/-su/-sü'.
When combining possessive and case suffixes, possessive ALWAYS precedes case.

quiz.question: Complete the phrase: 'mənim qələm___' (my pen).
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular possessive suffix after a consonant with front vowel 'ə' is '-im'.

quiz.question: Complete the phrase: 'onun maşın___' (his/her car).
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular possessive suffix after consonant is '-ı⁴', hence 'maşını'.

quiz.question: Complete the phrase: 'sizin otağ___' (your pl. room).
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person plural possessive suffix is '-ınız⁴' (here '-ınız' following 'a'). Note root 'otaq' shifts q->ğ.

quiz.question: Complete the phrase: 'onun ana___' (his mother).
quiz.explanation: Vowel stems take '-sı⁴' in the 3rd person possessive, yielding 'anası'.

tip: When 1st or 2nd person possessive suffixes attach to nouns ending in 'k' or 'q', the consonant lenites: 'ürək' -> 'ürəyim', 'otaq' -> 'otağım'.

title: Definite Past Tense (-dı⁴)
subtitle: Conjugating witnessed and definite past actions with -dı/-di/-du/-dü
keyPoint: The definite past suffix -dı⁴ attaches to the verb root and takes special personal endings to indicate completed past actions.

examples.en: O, sualı çox cəld başa düşdü.

mistakes.note: Definite specific time markers like 'dünən' (yesterday) strongly require the definite past '-dim', not the indefinite past '-mişəm'.
Because 'gəl-' has front vowel 'ə', the 1st person plural past marker must end in '-k' ('gəldik'), not back '-q'.
The personal ending for 'mən' in the definite past is just '-m', not predicative '-am'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Biz dünən bazara ___' (we went).
quiz.explanation: 'Biz' takes the past 1st-person plural ending '-ik' / '-uq' / '-k' following '-di', yielding 'getdik'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Sən bu kitabı ___?' (did you read?).
quiz.explanation: 2nd person singular 'sən' takes root + '-du' + '-n' -> 'oxudun'.

quiz.question: Select the correct negation: 'O dərsi ___' (he did not understand).
quiz.explanation: Negation inserts '-ma⁴' before the tense marker: root 'anla-' + '-ma-' + '-dı' -> 'anlamadı'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mən sənə məktub ___' (I wrote).
quiz.explanation: 1st person singular 'mən' takes '-m' after the tense suffix '-dı' -> 'yazdım'.

tip: The definite past tense uses special concise personal endings (-m, -n, —, -q/-k, -nız⁴, -lar²) instead of the longer predicative copular suffixes.

title: Present Continuous Tense (-ır⁴)
subtitle: Expressing actions happening right now or ongoing routines
keyPoint: The present continuous suffix -ır/-ir/-ur/-ür attaches to verb stems to describe current actions or regular habits.

cells: he/she does not write / isn't writing

mistakes.note: In the negative present continuous, the negation suffix fuses as -mır⁴, dropping the standard broad vowel -ma/-mə.
When the stem ends in 'ə' (işlə-), the vowel harmony and buffer sound shift it into işləyir or işləyir depending on dialect; standard written form keeps the vowel and adds 'y'.
In standard Azerbaijani, questions are formed via intonation rather than the Turkish question particle -mi.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I am writing' in Azerbaijani?
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person singular ending is -(y)am/-(y)əm, making 'yaz-ır-am'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Onlar indi kinoya ___.' (They are not going)
quiz.explanation: 3rd-person plural takes -lər after the negative continuous suffix -mir, producing 'getmirlər'.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly fills the blank: 'Sən harada ___?' (Where do you live?)
quiz.explanation: The subject 'sən' requires the 2nd-person singular suffix -san, giving 'yaşayırsan'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative form of 'oxuyur' (he reads):
quiz.explanation: The continuous negative fuses to -mır⁴. For 'oxu-', the harmonic match is 'oxumur'.

tip: Azerbaijani does not use a question particle like Turkish 'mi'; simply use rising pitch at the end of the sentence to turn any statement into a question!

title: Noun Compounds (İzafət II and III)
subtitle: Differentiating general noun compounds from specific possessive pairs
keyPoint: Indefinite compounds leave the first noun bare, while definite possessive constructions require the genitive case on the first noun.

useCases.label: Types and categories of objects (İzafət II)

examples.en: O, hər gün avtobus dayanacağında gözləyir.
Mən bu gün çay dəsmalı aldım.

mistakes.note: Compound nouns (İzafət II) must attach the 3rd-person possessive suffix -(s)ı to the second noun.
When referring to a specific item belonging to a specific object, the first noun must take the genitive ending -(n)ın.
When the possessor is a personal pronoun, the possessed noun must take the matching personal possessive suffix (-m, not bare).

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly means 'sun glasses' (as a generic item)?
quiz.explanation: İzafət II leaves the first noun bare and gives the second noun the 3rd-person suffix: 'günəş eynəyi'.

quiz.question: Complete the definite possessive phrase: 'Bu ___ qapısıdır.' (the house's)
quiz.explanation: Definite noun compounds (İzafət III) require the genitive case -(n)ın on the possessor noun: 'evin'.

quiz.question: How do you translate 'Anar's pen'?
quiz.explanation: Anar's specific pen is an İzafət III construction: 'Anarın qələmi'.

quiz.question: What is the correct form for 'water bottle'?
quiz.explanation: Compound nouns take the 3rd-person suffix -(s)ı after vowels, resulting in 'su şüşəsi'.

tip: Think of İzafət II (çay stəkanı) as a single concept/compound word, whereas İzafət III (Muradın stəkanı) shows true ownership.

title: Definite vs. Indefinite Future Tenses (-acaq vs. -ar)
subtitle: Certain plans (-acaq⁴) versus hypothetical predictions or offers (-ar²)
keyPoint: Use -acaq⁴ for firm plans and inevitable facts, but -ar² for assumptions, uncertain predictions, polite requests, and offers.

cells: I might go / I would go

examples.en: Biz gələn həftə yeni evə köçəcəyik.
Narahat olma, hər şey yaxşı olar.
O, imtahandan mütləq yüksək qiymət alacaq.
O bu sözü heç vaxt deməz.

mistakes.note: When expressing a concrete scheduled plan for tomorrow, use the definite future -acaq/-əcək instead of -ar.
The negative indefinite future simplifies to -mar² in the 1st person, and -maz² for other persons (not -mayar).
Intervocalic 'k' softens to 'y' before personal vowel endings: gələcək + ik = gələcəyik.

quiz.question: Which verb form denotes a firm, tickets-bought plan: 'Biz sabah İtaliyaya ___'?
quiz.explanation: Planned, definite future actions use -acaq/-əcək: 'gedəcəyik'.

quiz.question: How do you politely ask someone to pass the bread: 'Çörəyi verə ___?'
quiz.explanation: Polite requests use the indefinite future suffix -ar/-ər: 'verərsiniz?'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative indefinite form: 'O heç vaxt yalan ___.' (He wouldn't lie)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd-person negative of the indefinite future uses -maz/-məz: 'danışmaz'.

quiz.question: Translate the assumption: 'Maybe he will come.' -> 'Bəlkə o ___.'
quiz.explanation: Speculations paired with words like 'bəlkə' (maybe) naturally trigger the indefinite future: 'gələr'.

tip: Remember consonant mutation: the 'q' in -acaq turns to 'ğ' (yazacağam) and 'k' in -əcək turns to 'y' (gələcəyəm) when adding 1st-person suffixes.

title: Evidential / Indefinite Past Tense (-mış⁴ vs. -ıb⁴)
subtitle: Unwitnessed occurrences, deductions, and fast narrative recounting
keyPoint: Use -mış⁴ when relaying hearsay or newly discovered outcomes, while -ıb⁴ functions as an efficient past narrative and resultative marker.

useCases.label: Information learned from someone else
useCases.example: Deyirlər ki, o, yeni iş tapıb.

useCases.label: Realizing an event after seeing its result
Chaining actions in storytelling
useCases.example: O, otağa daxil olub pəncərəni açdı.

examples.en: Eşitdim ki, Murad imtahanı uğurla verib.
Gecə güclü külək əsib, ağaclar aşıb.
Sən demə, o da bu məktəbdə oxuyurmuş.

mistakes.note: If you witnessed or directly took part in a concrete past event, use the definite past (-dı⁴), not the evidential form.
The suffix -ıb⁴ is strictly forbidden with the 1st person (mən/biz); use -mış⁴ instead.
In modern spoken and written Azerbaijani, dropping the archaic copula suffix -dir is standard.

quiz.question: Why is 'Mən çörək alıbam' incorrect?
options: The verb stem 'al-' cannot take past tense
quiz.explanation: The suffix -ıb⁴ cannot combine with 1st-person personal endings (mən/biz); you must say 'almışam'.

quiz.question: Complete the hearsay sentence: 'Eşitdim ki, o universitetə daxil ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'olub' (or 'olmuşdur') expresses indirect evidentiality/hearsay ('I heard that...').

quiz.question: Which sentence expresses realizing you forgot your keys upon checking your pocket?
quiz.explanation: -mış⁴ conveys realization of a past action through present evidence: 'unutmuşam'.

quiz.question: Select the correct negative evidential past form for 'O yazdı' (hearsay: 'He hasn't written'):
quiz.explanation: The negative evidential past form combines -ma/-mə with -yıb/-yib: 'yazmayıb'.

tip: Golden rule: Never attach 1st-person endings (-am / -ıq) to -ıb! For 'I did / We did' (evidential), always pick -mışam / -mışıq.

title: Postpositions and Case Government (Qoşmalar)
subtitle: Mastering words placed after nouns to establish direction, cause, and time
keyPoint: Azerbaijani uses postpositions rather than prepositions, and each postposition requires its preceding noun to take a specific case.

examples.en: Hava soyuq olduğuna görə palto geyindim.

mistakes.note: Postpositions that take bare nouns (like üçün) require personal pronouns to be in the genitive case: 'mənim üçün', 'sənin üçün'.
Make sure 'sonra' governs the ablative case: 'dərsdən sonra' (never 'dərs sonra').
Postpositions already assign directional meaning; do not duplicate case suffixes onto 'tərəf'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the right form: 'Biz saat beşdən ___ gözləyirik.' (since)
quiz.explanation: The postposition 'bəri' (since) governs the ablative case (-dan/-dən): 'beşdən bəri'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'like you' in Azerbaijani?
quiz.explanation: 'kimi' governs nominative on regular nouns but genitive on personal pronouns: 'sənin kimi'.

quiz.question: Which case is required before the postposition 'görə' (because of / according to)?
quiz.explanation: 'görə' always takes the dative case (e.g., 'buna görə', 'sənə görə').

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase: '___ əvvəl zəng elə.' (before coming)
quiz.explanation: 'əvvəl' requires the ablative case suffix -dən: 'gəlməkdən əvvəl'.

tip: Watch out for personal pronouns: while nouns stay nominative before 'üçün' and 'kimi' (uşaq üçün), pronouns MUST switch to genitive (mənim üçün, onun kimi).

title: Necessity and Obligation Moods (-malı vs. Gərək / Lazım)
subtitle: Express internal duty with suffixes or external necessity with modal words
keyPoint: Attach the suffix -malı/-məli directly to a verb stem for personal obligation, or use modal nouns like lazım and gərək with an infinitive or subjunctive for general requirements.

cells: I must go / I ought to go
It is necessary to read a lot

useCases.label: General Necessity
useCases.example: Sağlam qalmaq üçün idman etmək lazımdır.

examples.en: Bu məsələni tez həll etmək lazımdır.
İmtahana girmək üçün şəxsiyyət vəsiqəsi vacibdir.

mistakes.note: When using lazım with an infinitive for a specific person, the subject must take the dative case (mənə, sənə).
While 'deyil' can negate -malı in the present, past negated obligations usually attach the negative -ma/-mə directly to the stem.
The particle 'gərək' triggers the optative/subjunctive mood suffix (-a/-ə), not the indicative present tense.

quiz.question: Every citizen ___ respect the state laws.
quiz.explanation: The obligation suffix -malı/-məli with the 3rd person suffix -dır expresses 'must/ought to'.

quiz.question: To learn a language, it is necessary ___ words every day.
quiz.explanation: General impersonal necessity uses the infinitive (-mək) followed by 'lazımdır'.

quiz.question: We ___ today; the weather is awful.
quiz.explanation: 'Getməməliyik' means 'we must not go', incorporating the negative -mə- into -məli- with 1st person plural -yik.

quiz.question: You ought to ___ your doctor regularly (using gərək).
quiz.explanation: The modal word 'gərək' pairs naturally with the 2nd person singular optative form 'görəsən'.

tip: Distinguish personal responsibility from impersonal rules: use '-malı' when pointing directly at the doer, and 'infinitive + lazımdır' when stating an impersonal requirement.

title: Imperative and Optative Moods (Əmr və Arzu Şəkilləri)
subtitle: Issue direct instructions and utter polite wishes or suggestions
keyPoint: The imperative mood employs distinct person-specific endings with no overt suffix on the bare stem for 'you (singular)', whereas the optative utilizes -(y)a/-(y)ə to convey wishes and suggestions.

useCases.label: Heartfelt Wish
useCases.example: Kaş ki, sən də bizimlə gələsən.

examples.en: Zəhmət olmasa, mənə bir stəkan su verin.
Kaş bu gün anam bizə gələ.

mistakes.note: '-in/-ın/-un/-ün' is reserved for the polite or plural 'siz'; the bare stem is used for informal singular 'sən'.
In speech, the 1st person imperative/optative ending '-aq/-ək' functions as 'let us', not as an indicative question without context.
The particle 'kaş' (if only) obligatorily governs the optative mood ending (-a/-ə), not the present indicative.

quiz.question: Please ___ the window, it is cold inside (polite).
quiz.explanation: The polite plural imperative takes -(y)ın/-(y)in/-(y)un/-(y)ün, yielding 'bağlayın'.

quiz.question: Let him ___ here and wait for us.
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular imperative suffix is -sın/-sin/-sun/-sün.

quiz.question: If only you would ___ the exam successfully!
quiz.explanation: The optative 2nd person singular suffix -(y)asın/-(y)əsən attaches to 'keç' to make 'keçəsən'.

quiz.question: Let's ___ lunch together!
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural imperative/hortative suffix is -(y)aq/-(y)ək, making 'yeyək'.

tip: Use the bare verb root for casual orders to friends ('Bax!'), but always add '-ın/-in' for politeness and respect ('Baxın!').

title: Converbs for Sequential and Manner Actions (-(y)ıb and -(y)araq)
subtitle: Chain consecutive actions and depict simultaneous manner elegantly
keyPoint: The converb -(y)ıb expresses an action completed immediately before the main verb, while -(y)araq expresses the manner or a simultaneous background action.

useCases.label: Manner of Action
useCases.example: Müəllim təbəssüm edərək suala cavab verdi.

useCases.label: Without Doing Something
useCases.example: O heç nə deməyərək otaqdan uzaqlaşdı.

examples.en: Uşaq qaça-qaça yox, qaçaraq yanımıza gəldi.
O, musiqiyə qulaq asaraq rəsm çəkir.

mistakes.wrong: Mən kitabı oxudum və rəfə qoydum.
mistakes.note: While 'və' is grammatically possible, native Azerbaijani strongly prefers the converb -(y)ıb to chain related clauses sharing a subject.
If crying describes the manner while speaking, use -(y)araq; -(y)ıb implies she cried first, stopped, and then spoke.
The -(y)ıb converb is predominantly restricted to clauses having identical grammatical subjects.

quiz.question: He turned off the computer and ___ to sleep.
quiz.explanation: Turned off and then left is a direct sequence of actions sharing a subject, requiring -(y)ıb.

quiz.question: She explained the rules ___ carefully.
quiz.explanation: The suffix -(y)araq indicates manner ('by explaining' / 'explaining').

quiz.question: We did our homework and ___ outside.
quiz.explanation: 'Edib çıxdıq' smoothly joins two sequential actions done by 'biz'.

quiz.question: He left the meeting without ___ anything.
quiz.explanation: The negative converb -mayaraq/-məyərək conveys 'without saying'.

tip: Avoid repeating 'və' (and) across sequential sentences; replacing the first conjugated verb with '-(y)ıb' instantly makes your speech sound natural and fluent.

title: Temporal Converbs (-anda, -dıqda, -ınca)
subtitle: Build complex 'when', 'while', and 'as soon as' time clauses
keyPoint: Attach -anda/-əndə for conversational 'when', -dıqda⁴ for formal temporal contexts, and -(y)ınca⁴ to express the exact boundary 'as soon as' or 'until'.

useCases.label: Formal Temporal Trigger
useCases.example: Təhlükə yarandıqda dərhal xilasedicilərə məlumat verin.

examples.en: Zəng çalınanda bütün şagirdlər sinfə qaçdı.
Qapını açanda qarşısında köhnə dostunu gördü.

mistakes.wrong: Nə vaxt mən gəldim, o yatmışdı.
mistakes.note: Do not translate English 'when' with the interrogative 'nə vaxt'; temporal subordinate clauses require converb suffixes like -anda.
Subordinate temporal converb clauses must keep their subject inside or before the converb clause.
The postposition 'qədər' (until) pairs with the dative participle -(y)an-a, whereas -(y)ınca already incorporates the meaning of 'until/as soon as' on its own.

quiz.question: Call me ___ you reach the airport.
quiz.explanation: The everyday temporal converb 'when you arrive' is formed with -(y)anda: 'çatanda'.

quiz.question: In official notices: '___ an alarm, keep calm.'
quiz.explanation: The suffix -dıqda/-dikdə/-duqda/-dükdə conveys formal or written 'upon/when'.

quiz.question: Wait here ___ the rain stops.
quiz.explanation: The converb -(y)ınca implies 'until / as soon as the event occurs'.

quiz.question: ___ entered the room, everyone stood up.
quiz.explanation: 'Girəndə' correctly creates the temporal clause 'When (he/she) entered'.

tip: Think of -anda as the everyday, conversational way to say 'when', and save -dıqda for official writing, news, or formal speeches.

title: Participles and Relative Clauses (-an, -dığı, -acaq)
subtitle: Build subject and object relative clauses that precede nouns
keyPoint: Azerbaijani relative clauses precede the head noun using the subject participle -(y)an or the object participle -dığı (with possessive agreement).

cells: Görəcəyim iş (The work I will do)

examples.en: Məclisdə oturan qonaqlar musiqiyə qulaq asırdılar.

mistakes.wrong: Adam kim qapını açdı, mənim dostumdur.
mistakes.note: Azerbaijani does not use relative pronouns like 'kim' (who) or 'hansı ki' (which) in native syntax; relative clauses precede the head noun with participles.
When the head noun is the object of the clause ('the book that I read'), use the -dığı + possessive participle, not the subject participle -an.
If the head noun is the subject performing the action ('the person going with us'), use -(y)an, not -dığı.

quiz.question: The boy ___ in the garden is my brother.
quiz.explanation: The boy is the subject of the playing action, so the subject participle -(y)an is required: 'oynayan'.

quiz.question: The meal that my mother ___ was delicious.
quiz.explanation: The food is the direct object of mother's cooking, so -dığı + 3rd person possessive (-i) -> 'bişirdiyi' is used.

quiz.question: The car that we will ___ tomorrow is new.
quiz.explanation: A prospective action on an object uses -(y)acaq + possessive ending: 'alacağımız'.

quiz.question: ___ should register at the front desk.
quiz.explanation: 'Gələnlər' is the substantivized participle meaning 'those who arrived / come'.

tip: Ask yourself: Is the noun doing the action? Use '-an' (e.g. 'yazan qız' = the girl who writes). Is the noun receiving the action? Use '-dığı' (e.g. 'yazdığı məktub' = the letter that she wrote).

title: Real and Unreal Conditionals (-sa² and İdi / İsə)
subtitle: Express real conditions and hypothetical counterfactuals
keyPoint: Attach the two-way suffix -sa/-sə directly to the verb stem for real present or future conditions, but attach it to past or imperfective stems combined with the past copula idi to convey unreal counterfactuals.

cells: If he comes, we will see.
If I had known, I would have come.
If I had seen, I would have said.

useCases.label: Real Future Condition
useCases.example: Sabah hava yaxşı olsa, parka gedəcəyik.

examples.en: Pulum çox olsaydı, yeni ev alardım.
Dərsi yaxşı oxusan, imtahanı asanlıqla keçərsən.
Əgər o vaxt zəng etsəydin, görüşərdik.

mistakes.note: Azerbaijani conditional clauses require the conditional suffix -sa/-sə rather than the future tense -acaq.
In unreal counterfactual apodoses (result clauses), use the aorist past (-ardı/-ərdi) rather than the future past.
When using idi with a vowel-ending suffix like -sə, insert the buffer consonant 'y' or fuse as -səydi.

quiz.question: If you study hard, you will pass the exam: 'Çox ___, imtahanı verəcəksən.'
quiz.explanation: A real future condition takes the direct conditional suffix -san (2nd person singular of -sa).

quiz.question: If I had money right now, I would buy that car: 'Pulum ___, o maşını alardım.'
quiz.explanation: An unreal hypothetical conditional uses the compound past conditional suffix -saydı.

quiz.question: If we hurry, we can catch the bus: '___, avtobusa çatarıq.'
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural real condition suffix is -sək.

quiz.question: If she had called me yesterday, I would have answered: 'Dünən mənə zəng ___, cavab verərdim.'
quiz.explanation: Counterfactual conditions referring to past unrealized events require -səydi.

tip: The introductory conjunction 'əgər' (if) is optional in Azerbaijani; the suffix -sa/-sə alone fully conveys the conditional meaning.

title: Verbal Nouns in -maq² and -ma² with Case and Possessives
subtitle: Nominalize actions and apply case markers and possessives
keyPoint: Use -maq for abstract infinitives receiving grammatical cases, but switch to the short verbal noun -ma/-mə whenever possessive person suffixes must be attached.

cells: I do not want his leaving.

useCases.label: Verbal Noun as Object with Possessive

examples.en: Biz dərsi vaxtında bitirməkdən məmnun olduq.

mistakes.note: When the possessed verbal noun functions as a definite direct object, it requires the accusative case suffix -ı/-i/-u/-ü.
Use the short verbal noun (-mə + -yin) for possessives; the infinitive -mək cannot directly take possessive personal suffixes without mutating or sounding ungrammatical.
Intervocalic 'q' in -maq softens to 'ğ' before vowel suffixes like the dative -a.

quiz.question: Your coming early made us very glad: 'Sənin tez ___ bizi çox sevindirdi.'
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular possessive attaches to the short verbal noun stem -mə as -məyin.

quiz.question: He started to learn the Azerbaijani language: 'O, Azərbaycan dilini ___ başladı.'
quiz.explanation: The verb 'başlamaq' governs the dative case (-a/-ə), transforming -mək into -məyə.

quiz.question: I am tired of waiting here: 'Burada ___ bezdim.'
quiz.explanation: The verb 'bezmək' requires the ablative case suffix -dən/-dan on the verbal noun.

quiz.question: We did not want his departure: 'Biz onun ___ istəmədik.'
quiz.explanation: Third person singular possessive (-si) plus the accusative case marker (-ni) yields -məsini.

tip: Remember: -maq softens to -mağ- before vowels (oxumaq -> oxumağa), while -ma takes -y- before 2nd person possessives (gəlmə-y-in).

title: Complex Verb Voice Derivations
subtitle: Stack passive, causative, reciprocal, and reflexive voice suffixes
keyPoint: Stack voice suffixes in standard sequence onto the verb root—reflexive/reciprocal or causative, followed by passive—to alter transitivity and agency.

mistakes.note: Use -ıl⁴ for passive when the root ends in a consonant other than 'l'; -ın⁴ is reserved for reflexive or specific roots.
Ensure stacked suffixes follow the strict morphological order: Root + Causative (-dir) + Passive (-il).
Reciprocal verbs often change case government; 'baxışmaq' governs the dative (-ə), not the accusative (-i).

quiz.question: The historical building was restored last year: 'Tarixi bina keçən il ___.'
quiz.explanation: The causative -dir stacked with passive -il yields 'təmir etdirildi' (was made to be restored).

quiz.question: The two old friends met after many years: 'İki köhnə dost illər sonra ___.'
quiz.explanation: The reciprocal voice suffix -(ü)ş indicates mutual action: görüşmək (to meet each other).

quiz.question: The child washed and prepared himself: 'Uşaq səhər tezdən yuyunub ___.'
quiz.explanation: The reflexive suffix -(i)n indicates an action performed on oneself: geyindi (he dressed himself).

quiz.question: All the tasks were completed on time: 'Bütün tapşırıqlar vaxtında ___.'
quiz.explanation: The passive form of yetirmək is yetirilmək; with past tense it becomes yerinə yetirildi.

tip: If a verb stem ends in the letter 'l' (like 'al-' to take), the passive suffix shifts from -ıl to -ın (alındı, not alıldı) to prevent awkward consonant repetition.

title: Compound Verb Formations with Bilmək, Başlamaq, and Qalmaq
subtitle: Convey potentiality, inchoative starts, and continuous duration
keyPoint: Combine a lexical verb ending in -a/-ə or -maq with auxiliary verbs like bilmək (ability), başlamaq (initiation), or qalmaq (uninterrupted duration).

useCases.label: Ability and Possibility
useCases.example: Mən bu çətin suala cavab verə bilərəm.

useCases.label: Stupefied or Persistent State
useCases.example: Gözlənilməz xəbəri eşidəndə donub qala qaldı.

examples.en: Açarımı tapa bilmədiyim üçün qapıda qaldım.
Müəllim daxil olanda hamı susmağa başladı.

mistakes.note: Bilmək requires the gerund suffix -a/-ə on the preceding verb, never the full infinitive -mək.
Başlamaq requires its preceding verbal noun to carry the dative case suffix (-mağa/-məyə).
To convey continuing in an uninterrupted, transfixed state, use -a/-ə qalmaq rather than bilmək.

quiz.question: Can you speak Azerbaijani fluently?: 'Sən azərbaycanca səlis ___?'
quiz.explanation: Potentiality (can/able to) uses the gerund stem -a/-ə followed by inflected bilmək: danışa bilirsənmi.

quiz.question: It started raining suddenly: 'Birdən yağış ___.'
quiz.explanation: Inchoative aspect (started doing) combines the dative infinitive -mağa with başlamaq.

quiz.question: We looked in astonishment after the departing car: 'Gedən maşının arxasınca ___.'
quiz.explanation: The durative aspect suffix -a/-ə qalmaq describes staying transfixed in an action: baxa qaldıq.

quiz.question: Unfortunately, I cannot help you today: 'Təəssüf ki, bu gün sizə kömək ___.'
quiz.explanation: Negative present ability is formed with gerund -ə + bilmirəm: kömək edə bilmirəm.

tip: In everyday speech, 'gələ bilmirəm' (I cannot come) is frequently contracted into 'gələmmirəm', merging the potential gerund and negative marker.

title: Complex Clausal Nominalization with -dığı üçün and -dığı halda
subtitle: Formulate sophisticated causal, concessive, and contrastive subordinate clauses
keyPoint: Attach the relative participle -dıq⁴ followed by possessive agreement suffixes to nominalize embedded clauses before postpositions like üçün (reason) or halda (concession/contrast).

cells: Because he got sick, he did not come.
Although he knows, he stays silent.
When he arrived home, he called.
While he works, his brother sleeps.

useCases.label: Expressing Definite Cause
useCases.example: Qatar gecikdiyi üçün iclasa vaxtında çatmadıq.

useCases.label: Concessive Contrast ('Although')
useCases.example: Çox çalışdığı halda, istədiyi nəticəni ala bilmədi.

useCases.label: Personal Subject Nominalization
useCases.example: Sənin bu qərarı verdiyin üçün çox şadam.

examples.en: Hava çox soyuq olduğu üçün qalın geyindik.
Dəvət edildiyi halda, ziyafətə gəlməkdən imtina etdi.
Mənim xəbərim olmadığı üçün heç nə deyə bilmədim.
Həqiqəti bildiyiniz halda niyə yalan danışırsınız?
Vaxtımız az olduğu üçün söhbəti qısa kəsdik.

mistakes.wrong: Mən gəldiyim üçün o sevindi, çünki mən gəldim.
mistakes.note: Do not duplicate the reason clause by pairing the postpositional nominalization (-dığım üçün) with the conjunction çünki in the same sentence.

mistakes.wrong: O bildiyi üçün danışmır, amma bilir.
mistakes.note: Use 'halda' (not 'üçün') after the inflected participle to mean 'although' or 'even though'.

mistakes.wrong: Sən dediyin üçün deyil, sənin dediyin halda.
mistakes.note: Ensure person agreement matches the agent: 'sənin dediy-in üçün' (2nd person singular -in).

quiz.question: Because we missed the bus, we took a taxi: 'Avtobusa ___ görə taksi tutduq.'
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural participle form gecik-diyimiz followed by görə/üçün expresses 'because we were late'.

quiz.question: Although he exercised every day, he did not lose weight: 'Hər gün idman ___ arıqlaya bilmədi.'
quiz.explanation: The nominalized participle with 'halda' (etdiyi halda) forms the concessive meaning 'although he exercised'.

quiz.question: Since I did not have your phone number, I could not call you: 'Sənin nömrən ___ zəng edə bilmədim.'
quiz.explanation: Negative participle ol-ma-dığ-ı followed by üçün conveys 'because it was not present'.

quiz.question: Even though you knew the answer, why did you not raise your hand?: 'Cavabı ___ niyə əl qaldırmadın?'
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular concessive construction is bildiyin halda (although you knew).

tip: The suffix -dıq⁴ acts like an adjective or noun stem; when you attach a possessive suffix, the final 'q' or 'k' regularly softens to 'ğ' or 'y' (yazdığım, gördüyün, bildiyi).
